On Sun, Jul 18, 2027 at 09:25 Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Oliver — thanks for the quick heads up and the traces. I'm escalating to infra/serving now (cc'd). We'll triage immediately and follow up with an ETA within 30 minutes.

Quick findings from a first-pass on the traces and runtime metrics:
- The runtime process shows long stalls inside KV-cache lookup codepaths during high-concurrency lanes. Stalls correlate with batches that include mixed prefix keys (recent routing change introduced more heterogeneous prefixes in the same batch).
- Observed head-of-line (HOL) blocking: a stalled request holding a batch lock prevents others in the lane from making progress; this increases tail latency and amplifies backend timeouts.
- Simultaneous small (~1–4 token) requests cause frequent cache evictions (LRU churn) in the per-shard KV store — indicative of cache thrash when many small prefixes are mixed in the same working set.
- Reproduced locally with a synthetic workload that mirrors Headway's request skew; enabling strict lane isolation for hot prefixes removes the p99 spike.

Immediate mitigations to push now (order matters):
1) Disable prefix-level KV caching for the affected model variant (config toggle) — low risk, immediate effect on cache churn.
2) Reduce per-batch size from 64 -> 24 for the affected instance group to limit HOL coupling while we stabilize.
3) Apply a temporary per-request KV timeout (200ms) to fail fast instead of blocking the entire batch.

I'll prepare a small config patch and a hotfix rollout. Attaching a config diff and a short summary PDF.

Attachments: kv-config-diff.patch, logs-summary.pdf

Monica

Subject: Update: headway incident — root cause & next steps

Oliver / Sarah — following up with a summary and next steps after yesterday's incident.

Root cause (short): 
- A recent runtime routing change increased mixing of prefix key spaces within the same batching lanes. That exposed a pathological interaction between our per-shard LRU KV cache and batch-level locking which led to HOL blocking when a long-running KV lookup stalled. The mixed small-request pattern from Headway exacerbated LRU churn which increased eviction pressure.

Immediate actions taken: 
- Disabled prefix-level KV caching for the affected model variant (canary -> full rollout completed at 10:12 PDT).
- Reduced batch size on the affected instance group from 64 to 24 during the day-of mitigation window.
- Applied per-request KV timeout to avoid blocking batch progress.

Status: Metrics returned to baseline after the prefix-cache disablement and batch-size change (p99 returned to ~220ms and 5xx dropped to <0.2%). We will keep the mitigations for 48 hours while we test a safer reconfiguration.

Planned follow-ups: 
- Engineering will ship a safer caching policy that isolates hot prefixes (expected in 5 business days).
- We'll provide an RCA document with logs and timelines (Jira SUP-3452).
- Offer: we will evaluate a one-time credit for the impacted window; Vivek will follow up with finance and your account team.

Attachments: logs-summary.pdf, kv-config-diff.patch

Please let me know if you'd like a 30-minute postmortem sync this week; we can include Monica and Dylan to walk through the technical details.

Irene
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
